<!--
PROMOTED TO THE BODY 2026-08-10 (Luciano) as Figure 5, and the set renumbered around it: the corner
figure became Figure 6 and the usage map Figure 7. This file was figure_6B_four.Rmd; the eight-member
own-tau_int companion (was figure_6BB.Rmd) is figure_5_S1.Rmd, this figure's supplement 1.
WHY IT IS A BODY FIGURE. Every other figure in the set is indexed by the DESIGN (channel count,
noise, sampling interval), which a reader of their own recording does not know. This one is indexed
by a number they measure on their own record with no model and no fit. The Introduction's closing
paragraph makes that offer and, until this promotion, nothing in the paper drew it.
WHAT WAS SETTLED WITH IT, and neither is to be re-opened without a reason:
  FOUR MEMBERS, not three. ILSE, INR, R, IR is the factorial of the two axes, and R is the only
  recursion-without-averaging member; with R dropped, INR is the only one-axis member left and the
  reader attributes the repair to the rest of the ladder in a lump, which 04_results explicitly
  declines to say ("the family cannot be ordered on a single scale").
  ONE SHARED Y, not a scale per panel. The vertical distance between members at the same x IS what
  switching likelihood buys, and per-panel scales destroy exactly that. Second reason, and it is the
  decisive one: IR's internal structure is the estimation floor of the statistic (1.043 +- 0.010,
  see figure_5_variant_2members.Rmd item 4), so a free axis draws the bootstrap at full panel height.
  The free-scale reading belongs to the supplement, which is what it is for.

The x is tau_int of the LEAST-SQUARES residual for every series, because that is what a reader has
before choosing a method; see the note in figure_5_variant_2members.Rmd for why that is the right
independent variable and for why tau_int is not self-referential.

WHY THESE FOUR. They are the 2x2 of the two axes: interval averaging (ILSE, INR have it in their
name; R does not) crossed with recursion (R and IR recurse, ILSE and INR do not). So the panel reads
as a factorial and a reader can see which of the two axes moves the distortion and which does not.

Labels follow figure_4.Rmd:329: nonlinearsqr_g = LSE, nonlinearsqr = ILSE, macro_NR = NR,
macro_INR = INR, macro_R = R, macro_MR = MR, macro_VR = VR, macro_IR = IR.

MEASURED 2026-08-10, and not written up anywhere else yet. The chunk below rebuilds all of it.

  THE DISTORTION HAS A THRESHOLD IN tau_int, BUT ONLY AT A FIXED SAMPLING RATE. Taking size >= 1.15
  as the criterion, the clean and the distorted cells separate without overlap at every sampling
  interval for both gating likelihoods that do not recurse (NR 7 of 7 intervals, INR 7 of 7). The
  two least-squares arms are messier, ILSE 5 of 7 (0.05 and 1 overlap) and LSE 4 of 7 (0.02, 0.5
  and 1). That difference is expected rather than awkward: 04_results.tex:283-289 already records
  that the least-squares ratio also carries the break of its constant-residual-variance premise,
  which is not an information-matrix-equality failure of the same kind.

  POOLED OVER INTERVALS NO THRESHOLD EXISTS, which is the same fact as item (2) of
  figure_5_variant_2members.Rmd.
  At criterion 1.15 the first distorted cell is at tau_int 1.074 while clean cells run to 1.861; at
  1.5 the pair is 1.205 and 1.861; at 2.0 it is 1.205 and 3.002. The reader needs two numbers.

  IR NEVER CROSSES IT IN SIZE, AND DOES CROSS IT IN SHAPE. Its size stays inside 0.982 to 1.077
  over all 294 source cells at both anchors, so zero cells reach 1.15 there. Its shape reaches
  1.419, and 28 of 294 cells sit at or above 1.15, every one of them at N_ch = 10 and the worst at
  noise 0.05, against an estimation floor of 1.043 +- 0.010. That is the Gaussian moment closure on
  the occupancy going at few channels, which 00_abstract.tex already states and which item (4) of
  figure_5_variant_2members.Rmd records as "the only departures are at N_ch = 10". WRITING THIS AS ONE NUMBER IS
  THE MISTAKE THIS FIGURE EXISTS TO PREVENT: a scalar summary cannot express a member that is right
  in the typical direction and wrong across directions, which is the same point item (5) makes
  about least squares at tau_int 1.80.

  R IS THE ONE THAT CAN BE MISREAD OFF THE PANEL, and the caption has to carry the reading. Pooled
  over the twelve noise levels its magnitude median is 1.01, next to IR's 1.00, so the panel LOOKS
  like it says R is calibrated while 04_results says R sits on a floor near 1.4 in k_off. Both are
  right and the dilution is the reason: mag is det(GIDM)^(1/p) over all six directions and most
  cells of the plane are at high noise where every member is calibrated. At noise 0.1 R reads a
  magnitude of 1.143 (1.09-1.24 by channel count) with an anisotropy of 1.19-1.29, so its bar
  reaches 1.48 and the failure is in the BAR, not in the point. This also closes the [OPEN] the
  four-member note carried against decisions.md's 1.46 for R: same pooling, and 1.46 is INR's
  median here, which is worth checking on its own given the NMR/INR history.
  Fraction of cells at or above 1.15 in SIZE, whole ladder:
  LSE 0.495, ILSE 0.524, NR 0.596, INR 0.600, R 0.148, MR 0.386, VR 0.333, IR 0.000.
  Medians and maxima of the size: ILSE 1.37 / 57.2, INR 1.46 / 33.1, NR 1.65 / 2217,
  R 1.01 / 1.26, IR 1.00 / 1.08.

  [CLOSED 2026-08-10] The [OPEN] that stood here, on R reading 1.01 against decisions.md's 1.46,
  is answered above: pooling over the noise axis, verified against the spectrum file. It was NOT
  a different anchor; mag at the sim anchor differs from mag at pool by less than the pooling
  effect. Do not reopen it as an anchor question.

  ONE EDIT THIS FILE STILL OWES, which does not change what the figure says.
  THE ILL-CONDITIONED CORNER IS NOT EXCLUDED and it sets the floor of the shared axis. R has
      six cells below magnitude 0.9 (minimum 0.590) and LSE twelve (minimum 0.074), and every one
      of them is at N_ch = 10^4 with interval_in_tau = 1, which is the corner Figure 4 already
      greys by a rule it owns: off-scale AND kappa > 3e4, figure_4_common.R:216-224, with the
      kappa in the same cell_scalars file this notebook already reads. ILSE, INR, NR and IR have
      no such cell. Applying that rule here costs a join and buys back about half a decade at the
      bottom of the axis, which is height for every panel; leaving it, the body figure draws as a
      measurement what Figure 4 greys as unidentified. In the drawing it is the low end of the
      lightest sweep of R and of LSE, the one at Delta_tilde = 1, which the lines now make traceable
      to its cell. The collapse chunk below already excludes it and says so.

ONE ROW OF FOUR PANELS, AND NOW FOR A MEASURED REASON. 2026-08-11 (Luciano). The encoding was taken
apart and put back the same day: a 7x4 grid with the sampling interval on the rows, the noise in
colour and the channel count in the symbol was drawn, looked at, and rejected. What settled it was
not the layout but a measurement made while arguing about it, and it is now Figure 5 supplement 2
(figure_5_S2.Rmd) with the numbers in the collapse chunk of figure_5_Nch.Rmd.

  THE NOISE AND THE CHANNEL COUNT ARE ONE AXIS, NOT TWO. They enter only through r = S_tilde/N_ch.
  Cells that share r at different (noise, N_ch) are separate simulations of different preparations,
  and at the same sampling interval they agree in tau_int to within 3.5% (median 1%) and in the
  distortion to a median of 1 to 2% for all eight members. Since tau_int is monotone in the noise at
  a fixed interval, that relation inverts: THE DISTORTION IS A FUNCTION OF tau_int AND OF THE
  SAMPLING INTERVAL, AND OF NOTHING ELSE. Those are exactly the two things this panel draws, x and
  colour. So the one row is not hiding two design axes, it is drawing the whole parameterization,
  and the check that it loses nothing is that at matched tau_int and matched interval the four
  channel counts agree to within 1.06 for ILSE, 1.15 for INR and 1.08 for IR (figure_5_Nch.Rmd).
  R reaches 1.81 and that is the ill-conditioned corner, the same one this file still owes an edit
  for. This argument is better than the one that used to stand here, and it is measured.

  WHAT THE 7x4 GRID BOUGHT, and why it was not enough. It drew the threshold where the threshold
  exists, within one sampling rate, which the crowd of marks in one row cannot show. But that fact
  is not written anywhere in the manuscript, so the body figure is not yet asked for it. If it ever
  is, the grid is in the git history of this file and figure_5_noise.Rmd is its sibling.

  THE LINES ARE THE ONE THING KEPT FROM THAT DETOUR. Each joins the noise sweep at one channel count
  and one interval, in order of noise and NOT of tau_int, which is the design order; tau_int is
  monotone in noise at 19 of the 28 (N_ch, interval) pairs and at the other 9 the single step in the
  wrong direction is at most 0.033 against sweeps spanning up to 16.4, so ordering by tau_int would
  hide the estimation error of the statistic by construction. Four lines are drawn per colour, one
  per channel count, and they land on each other: the collapse above is visible in the body figure
  without a panel spent on it, and the colour stops being a cloud and becomes seven trajectories.

Unchanged and still not to be re-opened: the four members, and the ONE SHARED Y.
The old x breaks (1, 1.2, 1.5, 2, 3) collided at 7 in; c(1, 2, 5, 10) fits and stays round.
Text sizes are written out rather than left to base_size: theme_bw scales axis text to 0.8 of the
base, so base_size = 8 was drawing the ticks at 6.4 pt, under eLife's floor of 7.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
suppressMessages({ library(tidyverse) })
```

```{r data}
source("noise_units.R")  # the one definition of S_tilde and of when to convert

SRC <- "../figure_4_source_data"
rd  <- function(f) read.csv(file.path(SRC, f), skip = 1, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

LAB  <- c(nonlinearsqr = "ILSE", macro_INR = "INR", macro_R = "R", macro_IR = "IR")
KEEP <- names(LAB)

# tick labels for the two decade-valued keys: plain from 0.01 to 100, powers outside. Parsed as
# plotmath by the scales below, so the exponents are set rather than spelled.
pw10 <- function(x) {
  e <- round(log10(x))
  ifelse(abs(e) <= 2, format(x, trim = TRUE, scientific = FALSE), sprintf("10^%d", e))
}

tau <- rd("figure_4_source_data_cell_scalars.csv") %>%
  filter(param == "lag", anchor == "pool", algo == "nonlinearsqr") %>%
  transmute(noise, Num_ch, interval_in_tau, tau_int = v)

spec <- rd("figure_4_source_data_spectrum.csv") %>%
  filter(anchor == "pool", algo %in% KEEP) %>%
  select(algo, param, noise, Num_ch, interval_in_tau, m) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = param, values_from = m)

dat <- spec %>%
  inner_join(tau, by = c("noise", "Num_ch", "interval_in_tau")) %>%
  filter(is.finite(mag), is.finite(aniso), mag > 0, aniso > 0) %>%
  mutate(lo = mag / aniso, hi = mag * aniso,
         member = factor(unname(LAB[algo]), levels = unname(LAB)),
         # the label is TEN TIMES S_tilde; convert here because this is where it is shown.
         S = dimensionless_noise(as.numeric(noise)),
         s = factor(pw10(S), levels = pw10(sort(unique(S)))),
         nch = factor(pw10(Num_ch), levels = pw10(sort(unique(Num_ch)))),
         d = factor(sprintf("%g", interval_in_tau),
                    levels = sprintf("%g", sort(unique(interval_in_tau)))),
         # one line per channel count and interval, joining that noise sweep in DESIGN order.
         sweep = interaction(interval_in_tau, Num_ch, drop = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(member, sweep, S)

cat(sprintf("figure_5: %d marks over %d cells in %d panels; per member: %s\n",
            nrow(dat), n_distinct(dat[c("noise","Num_ch","interval_in_tau")]),
            nlevels(dat$member),
            paste(sprintf("%s=%d", levels(dat$member), as.integer(table(dat$member))),
                  collapse = " ")))
cat(sprintf("each panel: %d lines (%d intervals x %d channel counts) over %d noise levels, S_tilde %g to %g\n",
            n_distinct(dat$sweep), nlevels(dat$d), nlevels(dat$nch), nlevels(dat$s),
            min(dat$S), max(dat$S)))
```

```{r render, fig.width = 7.0, fig.height = 3.8}
g <- ggplot(dat, aes(tau_int, mag, colour = d)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linewidth = 0.3, colour = "grey45") +
  geom_line(aes(group = sweep), linewidth = 0.3, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.75) +
  geom_point(size = 0.75) +
  facet_wrap(~ member, nrow = 1) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(1, 2, 5, 10), labels = c("1", "2", "5", "10")) +
  scale_y_log10(breaks = c(0.3, 1, 3, 10, 30, 100),
                labels = c("0.3", "1", "3", "10", "30", "100")) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(name = expression(widetilde(Delta)), option = "D", end = 0.92) +
  labs(x = expression("memory left in the least-squares residual,  "*tau[int]),
       y = "distortion of the reported information\n(point = size, bar = across directions)") +
  # sizes are written out rather than left to base_size, because theme_bw scales axis text to 0.8 of
  # it and eLife's floor of 7 pt is on the drawn text, not on the nominal base. Same set of sizes as
  # the other body figure of this paper, figure_4_layout.R:450-460.
  theme_bw(base_size = 8, base_family = "Helvetica") +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 7),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 8),
        legend.position = "right",
        legend.title = element_text(size = 8),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
        legend.key.height = unit(9, "pt"),
        legend.spacing.y = unit(3, "pt"),
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92", colour = NA),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 7))

ggsave("Figure_5.pdf", g, width = 7.0, height = 3.8, device = cairo_pdf)
g
```

```{r numbers}
dat %>% group_by(member) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            size_med = median(mag), size_min = min(mag), size_max = max(mag),
            shape_med = median(aniso), .groups = "drop") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% print(digits = 3)

cat("\nthreshold structure at criterion size >= 1.15, per member and sampling interval:\n")
dat %>% group_by(member, d) %>%
  summarise(tau_max_clean = suppressWarnings(max(tau_int[mag <  1.15])),
            tau_min_dist  = suppressWarnings(min(tau_int[mag >= 1.15])),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(separated = ifelse(is.finite(tau_max_clean) & is.finite(tau_min_dist),
                            tau_max_clean < tau_min_dist, NA)) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% print(digits = 3)
```

```{r collapse}
# THE ONE-DIMENSIONAL COLLAPSE, added 2026-08-11. This is what makes the two design axes drop out
# of the panel and it is what the Results paragraph and the Discussion both quote, so it is emitted
# here rather than asserted: at a FIXED sampling interval, is every quantity a function of
# S_tilde / N_ch alone? That ratio is the instrumental variance against the gating variance, since
# S_tilde is normalised by the single-channel signal and the gating variance goes as N_ch at fixed
# open probability. Reported as the worst within-group spread, max/min, over the groups holding it
# fixed; a spread of 1.00 would be an exact collapse.
# THE ILL-CONDITIONED CORNER IS EXCLUDED HERE and only here (N_ch 1e4 at Delta_tilde 1), by the same
# rule Figure 4 owns; leaving it in, R's group at that corner alone reports a spread of 1.6 that is
# a conditioning artefact and not a failure of the collapse. The figure above still draws it.
# GROUP ON THE DECADE, NOT ON THE RATIO ITSELF (fixed 2026-08-11). Every noise and every channel
# count in the battery is a power of ten, but the double S_tilde/N_ch is not bit-identical between
# (0.01, 10) and (0.1, 100): 0.1*0.1/10 and 1*0.1/100 differ in the last bit. Grouping on it splits
# matched cells apart, drops groups under the n() >= 3 filter, and understates the collapse. The
# integer exponent is exact. Same slip was made independently in figure_5_S2.Rmd on its first run.
coll <- dat %>%
  filter(!(Num_ch == 10000 & interval_in_tau == 1)) %>%
  mutate(ratio_key = round(log10(S)) - round(log10(Num_ch))) %>%
  group_by(member, d, ratio_key) %>%
  filter(n() >= 3) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), ratio = 10^first(ratio_key),
            tau_spread = max(tau_int) / min(tau_int),
            mag_spread = max(mag) / min(mag), .groups = "drop")

cat("\nCOLLAPSE ON S_tilde / N_ch at fixed sampling interval (worst spread over groups, max/min):\n")
coll %>% group_by(member) %>%
  summarise(groups = n(), cells = sum(n),
            tau_worst = max(tau_spread), mag_worst = max(mag_spread), .groups = "drop") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% print(digits = 3)

cat("\nsame, resolved by sampling interval, for the least-squares arm that sets the x:\n")
coll %>% filter(member == "ILSE") %>%
  select(d, ratio, n, tau_spread, mag_spread) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% print(digits = 3)
```
